answer: In a market where AI agents trade timber for tundra settlements, one identity per participant is a fable, so voting power follows escrowed stake instead of account count. Each unit of stake stays locked for 30 days and can back only one vote at a time. Splitting funds among a thousand fake agents creates no extra influence: to control a majority, an attacker must lock more capital than all honest voters combined, tying up funds for the full period.
